clue.text: Dopes come out as rotters do

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drug users emerging behave the way scoundrels do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotters' looks like slang for cads, but here it means things that rot.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that rot break down organically, which is exactly what decaying matter does.

clue.text: Welshman, gutted by party, redecorated

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: Dai is a stock Welsh man's name, short for David
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A Welshman, disembowelled by a political party, then redecorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' sounds violent but just strips the middle letter from the name; 'by' is only a link placing the party alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: To do up a room is an idiom for renovating or refurbishing it.

clue.text: Will race upset singular athlete?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the two words before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Will a one-off race upset an outstanding athlete?
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' seems to describe the athlete but simply supplies S.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Lewis is a celebrated American sprinter and long jumper, an example of a sportsman.

clue.text: Wicked poet's house contents

parts.note: Andrew Marvell was a 17th-century English poet; the apostrophe-s just links him to what follows

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters, with first and last dropped

explanation.surface: A villainous poet's household belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' looks like it means evil; it is slang approval.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, wicked is a term of praise meaning excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: One who resists work with model

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
a poser is someone who models or sits for a portrait

explanation.surface: A person who resists working alongside a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resisting a proposal is an opponent of it, a natural agent-noun sense.

clue.text: Without delay, say, loner dashed in

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the abbreviation for 'say'

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means when introducing an instance

indicators.note: dashed here means smashed, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Promptly, for instance, a solitary person rushed inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed in' reads as the loner rushing in, but 'dashed' scrambles the five letters (giving RELON) and 'in' puts them inside the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic phrase means before long, soon, i.e. shortly and with little wait.

clue.text: Lampoon francophone who resides in centre of Lisbon

indicators.note: resides in tells us the French word sits inside the central letters
the centre of a word is its middle letters, here two of them from a six-letter word

parts.note: qui is French for who, as a French speaker would say it

explanation.surface: A satirist mocks a French speaker who lives in central Lisbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A squib is a short satirical piece of writing, synonymous with a lampoon.

clue.text: Function without Latin

definitions.meaning: a trigonometric function, the ratio of opposite side to hypotenuse

explanation.surface: A function that works with no Latin involved.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the trigonometric ratio and the Latin preposition meaning lacking.

clue.text: Useful narrow section of a bone

indicators.note: a section of a phrase is a run of letters cut from inside its words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A handy slender cross-section of a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'section of' as indicator and 'bone' as definition, but the answer is an adjective, so 'of a bone' is the definition and 'section' alone signals the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the ulna, the forearm bone on the little-finger side.

clue.text: Cricket commentator has Edgbaston openers sent to Coventry

parts.note: Geoffrey Boycott, the former Yorkshire and England batsman, became a cricket commentator

indicators.note: openers are the opening letters, here the first two of the word

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator has the opening batsmen at Edgbaston ostracised.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgbaston is a Test cricket ground in Birmingham; 'openers' suggests batsmen but gives ED. To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Shunning someone and refusing all dealings with them is what both phrases describe.

clue.text: Old master more convinced when daughter replaces son

indicators.note: replaces signals that one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: surer is the comparative of sure, meaning more certain

explanation.surface: A sounder believer emerges when a daughter takes over from a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when daughter replaces son' swaps the S of SURER for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and printmaker, an example of a great early European artist.

clue.text: Start of parenthood: man and woman having swell time?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Reg is a man's name
Nancy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Parenthood begins when a couple have a wonderful time together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like 'excellent', but it means the belly swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is the months during which an expectant mother's belly grows, a playful description.

clue.text: PM, close to tears, hugged by non-U comedian

indicators.note: hugged by puts the letter inside the comedian's name
non-U means without the letter U; also a pun on upper-class usage

parts.note: Paul Merton is a British comedian, a regular on Have I Got News For You

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A prime minister, nearly in tears, gets embraced by a lowbrow comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' (not upper-class) removes U from PAUL MERTON, leaving PALMERTON; 'close to tears' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Palmerston was twice Britain's Prime Minister in the mid-19th century.

clue.text: Dash from Brazil's capital city

indicators.note: a word's capital is its initial letter

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A sprint from Brazil's capital to another city.
explanation.walkthrough: Brazil's capital is Brasília, not Rio, which is the trap; 'capital' gives only B.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of flair and vigour is a synonym for spirited liveliness.

clue.text: Get your glad rags on — and your skates

definitions.meaning: dress up smartly, so as to appear stylish
read with the opening 'Get your', this gives 'get your skates on', meaning hurry up

explanation.surface: Dress up for the party, and hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense borrows 'Get your' from the first: 'Get your skates on' means hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to dress smartly and, as a command, to be quick.

clue.text: Bad lad drew trailer

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naughty boy sketched a film preview or a towed vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' looks like a caravan or a film preview; it means one who trails behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trailing behind lags and loiters, a slowcoach.

clue.text: Bird only grabbing tail of saltwater fish

indicators.note: grabbing means the pair seizes a letter between them

parts.note: a dove is a bird
sole means only, as in 'the sole survivor'

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A bird only snatches the tail of a sea fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a flatfish of European waters, prized for eating.

clue.text: Monty's opponent with large cast in great ring

indicators.note: in puts the shortened general inside the abbreviation

parts.note: GT is an abbreviation for great

indicators.note: cast here means thrown away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Rommel, the German general, faced Montgomery (Monty) in North Africa
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Montgomery's adversary, with a large cast, appears in a great ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with large cast' looks theatrical, but means L is cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a reinforcing eyelet or washer, a small circular fitting.

clue.text: Old bird with no drink in singular performance

indicators.note: in puts the following words inside the bird

parts.note: the moa was a huge flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct
taken as written
a dram is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: An extinct bird with no drink inside it puts on a solo show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' means performed by one actor alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A monodrama is a play for one performer, a one-person show.

clue.text: View taking in both sides of unusual river

indicators.note: taking in means containing the letters inside the view

parts.note: a vista is a view or prospect

indicators.note: both sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A panorama encompassing both banks of a remarkable river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vistula is Poland's longest waterway, flowing through Warsaw to the Baltic.

clue.text: Paint tea party attendee almost eating blubber

indicators.note: eating means the shortened name surrounds the other piece
almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Alice attended the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland
to blubber is to cry noisily

explanation.surface: A guest at a tea party nearly devouring whale fat while painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like whale fat; it is the verb to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a type of quick-drying synthetic paint used by artists.

clue.text: Fancy man compared

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it
Ned is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A woman's lover is measured against another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy man' reads as a lover; split, it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Keen to accept book shedding some light

indicators.note: to accept means the word takes the letter into itself

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, i.e. to lament

explanation.surface: Eager to take on a book that illuminates things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager; it is the verb to mourn.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that flickers softly or glows gently over a surface.

clue.text: What's left behind?

parts.note: the clue reads as asking about a remainder, and also about one's backside

explanation.surface: What remains after the rest has gone?
explanation.definitionFit: A rump is both a remnant left over and an animal's hindquarters.

clue.text: Damp area avoided by chairman's follower

indicators.note: avoided by means the letter is left out of the follower

parts.note: a follower of Chairman Mao Zedong

explanation.surface: A soggy patch is steered clear of by the chairman's supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp and slightly wet are the same condition, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Walks made person fit

indicators.note: fit as a verb means to adjust or put into shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking walks made someone healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like the adjective healthy; it signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Promenades are leisurely strolls, especially along a seafront.

clue.text: Start from scratch and reach the highest point, say

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to peak is to reach a maximum

explanation.surface: Begin from nothing and climb to the summit, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a sounds-like signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something is to utter it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lively spot around year end

indicators.note: around means the word surrounds a letter

parts.note: to spot is to spy or catch sight of

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A vivacious spot appears near the end of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means active and nimble, especially of an older person.

clue.text: Showing sign of life, Orlando's dropped in without thinking

indicators.note: dropped in means the setter's contraction is put inside

parts.note: on means being shown, as a film is on
a pulse is a sign that someone is alive
Orlando is the setter, so Orlando's means 'I am', contracted

explanation.surface: Displaying vital signs, the setter popped in on a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting spontaneously is doing something on a sudden urge, unplanned.

clue.text: Rattle heard in part of cycle?

indicators.note: heard tells us the synonym is to be spoken, then spelt differently

parts.note: to rattle someone is to unsettle or faze them

explanation.surface: A rattling noise in a bit of bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycle' suggests a bike; it is a cycle such as the moon's.
explanation.definitionFit: A phase is a stage in a recurring sequence, as the moon has phases.

clue.text: Vestibule no good for posh people

indicators.note: no good means that letter is absent

parts.note: the gentry are the well-born upper class

explanation.surface: An entrance hall isn't good enough for the upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestibule is an entrance hall or lobby, the way into a building.

clue.text: Injured boxer not on one vessel or another

parts.note: cut means wounded

indicators.note: not means the following word is removed from the boxer

parts.note: Mike Tyson, the heavyweight boxer
taken as written
Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: A hurt boxer isn't aboard one ship or another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'another' means another vessel, following 'one vessel'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cutty Sark is a famous 19th-century tea clipper ship preserved at Greenwich.
